title: Hierarchical low rank matrices and error propagation

items.title: Finite cluster trees and geometric admissibility
items.statement: Defines balanced binary cluster trees over nonempty finite ordered row and column index sets with separate point assignments in a common Euclidean space, within-side diameters, cross-side distance, geometric admissibility, and recursive block-cluster refinement.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.3–1.6, 2.1–2.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.3.2–2.3.3

items.title: Size and depth of a balanced cluster tree
items.statement: A binary tree split by halves until clusters contain at most b indices has logarithmic depth and O(n/b) cluster nodes, with the stated leaf-size bounds.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§2.1.1–2.1.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.3.2

items.title: Block-cluster leaves partition the index-pair set
items.statement: The recursive admissible block-cluster tree has pairwise disjoint terminal rectangles whose union is the full row-index by column-index product.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.5, 2.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.3.2–2.3.3

items.title: Core-SVD recompression with rank and error tolerances
items.statement: Given a sum of low-rank factors, a rank cap k and a Frobenius tolerance, constructs a core-SVD truncation or returns tolerance-not-met.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§7.1–7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.2

items.title: H-matrix block representation
items.statement: Defines H-block storage with dense nearfield leaves and rank-k farfield factors, together with the represented block matrix.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.6, 2.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.1

items.title: Core-SVD recompression is best at the declared Frobenius tolerance
items.statement: The core-SVD factors have the singular values of the represented factor sum; the algorithm returns a minimum-rank approximation meeting tolerance under the cap, or certifies none exists.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§7.1–7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.2, Theorem 2.4.2.6

items.title: Nested H² cluster bases and interaction lists
items.statement: Defines row and column cluster bases, transfer matrices expressing nestedness, coupling matrices on admissible blocks, and bounded interaction lists.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), Chapter 9, §§9.1–9.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.6

items.title: H-matrix block matrix-vector multiplication
items.statement: Applies dense nearfield blocks and factorized farfield blocks on a finite disjoint block partition.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §1.6
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.3.5

items.title: Bottom-up low-rank recompression of block contributions
items.statement:
Let $b=(\tau,\sigma)$ be an admissible leaf of the finite block-cluster partition in [[def-hlr-and-h2-block-matrix-representations]]. A **factor-sum tree for $b$** is a finite rooted binary tree whose leaves carry factor pairs $U_v\in\mathbb F^{\tau\times r_v}$, $V_v\in\mathbb F^{\sigma\times r_v}$ for exact contributions $M_v=U_vV_v^*$; each internal node denotes the sum of the exact matrices denoted by its two children. Here $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $*$ is conjugate transpose, and all factors have the displayed finite dimensions.

**Input:** Such a tree, a rank cap $k\ge1$, node tolerances $\theta_v\ge0$ whose sum over all nodes is at most a requested block tolerance $\delta_b\ge0$, and the procedures/results [[alg-hlr-core-svd-recompression-with-tolerance]] and [[thm-hlr-core-svd-recompression-is-best-rank-tolerance]].

**Procedure:** Traverse the tree in postorder. At a leaf, pass its exact factor pair to core-SVD recompression. At an internal node, concatenate the returned child factor pairs, which represents the sum of the two child approximations, and pass that pair to core-SVD recompression. At every node use effective core cap $k_b=\min(k,|\tau|,|\sigma|)$ and tolerance $\theta_v$. If any call returns **tolerance-not-met**, return that status and node. On success, retain its factors and exact discarded-tail norm $\rho_v$. Define the node's reported error bound by $e_v=\rho_v$ at a leaf and $e_v=e_{v_1}+e_{v_2}+\rho_v$ at an internal node. If all calls succeed, return the root factors and $e_{\rm root}$. Then the root matrix has rank at most $k$ and its Frobenius error from the sum of all leaf contributions is at most $e_{\rm root}\le\sum_v\theta_v\le\delta_b$. A failed call means only that this chosen tree and its assigned local budgets did not produce a certificate; it does not assert that no rank-$k$ approximation of the full sum meets $\delta_b$.

Near blocks are not passed to this routine: they are assembled and stored densely and exactly. For a leaf carrying a dense contribution $D\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, use the exact factor pair $(D,I_n)$, where $I_n$ is the identity matrix; the routine may then compress it under its assigned tolerance.

The rank and error guarantees are proved in [[lem-hlr-bottom-up-recompression-error-bound]].

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§6.2, 7.1–7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.4.2–2.4.3

items.title: A separated Cauchy block has a geometric rank bound
items.statement: For points in separated one-dimensional intervals, the first r terms of the geometric kernel expansion give a rank-at-most-r matrix and an explicit entrywise and Frobenius error bound.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.2–1.3
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.2.2.1

items.title: Compress exact block LU factors with local tolerances
items.statement: Given exact block lower and upper factors of A, compress only admissible off-diagonal factor blocks, keep diagonal and nearfield blocks exact, and return local Frobenius error bounds.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§6.2, 7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.5

items.title: Bottom-up factor-sum recompression has the reported rank and Frobenius error bound

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§6.2, 7.1–7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.4.2–2.4.3

items.statement:
Use [[alg-hlr-bottom-up-recompression]] on a finite factor-sum tree for one admissible block over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, with exact arithmetic, rank cap $k\ge1$, node tolerances $\theta_v\ge0$, and $\sum_v\theta_v\le\delta_b$. Let $T_v$ be the subtree rooted at $v$, and let $M_v$ be the sum of its exact leaf contributions. Whenever all calls in $T_v$ succeed, the returned factors represent a matrix $\widehat M_v$ of rank at most $k$, and the reported bound satisfies
$$\|M_v-\widehat M_v\|_F\le e_v=\sum_{w\in T_v}\rho_w\le\sum_{w\in T_v}\theta_w.$$
In particular, if the routine succeeds at the root,
$$\operatorname{rank}(\widehat M_{\rm root})\le k,\qquad \|M_{\rm root}-\widehat M_{\rm root}\|_F\le e_{\rm root}=\sum_w\rho_w\le\sum_w\theta_w\le\delta_b.$$
Here $\rho_w$ is the exact discarded-tail norm returned at node $w$. A **tolerance-not-met** status at a node only means this chosen tree and these assigned local budgets did not produce the requested certificate; it does not assert that no rank-$k$ approximation of the exact full sum meets $\delta_b$.

items.title: Tolerance-controlled H-matrix block addition
items.statement: Adds dense nearfield blocks exactly and runs bottom-up recompression on a factor-sum tree for each far block, returning a certified local error bound or a tolerance failure.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §6.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.3

items.title: Tolerance-controlled H-matrix block product
items.statement: Forms the exact intermediate-cluster product contributions, keeps near outputs dense, and recompresses each far-output factor-sum tree bottom-up under local budgets.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §6.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.4

items.title: H-matrix block multiplication returns the represented matrix action
items.statement: The H-matrix block matvec algorithm returns exactly the action of the represented block matrix on every compatible vector.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §1.6
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.3.5

items.title: Nested-basis H² matrix-vector multiplication
items.statement: Uses upward and downward cluster-basis passes, admissible coupling products, and exact dense nearfield products.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), Chapter 9, §§9.1–9.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.6

items.title: Blockwise Frobenius errors propagate by disjoint block sums
items.statement: Local block tolerances yield a root-sum-square global Frobenius bound; addition and product errors obey explicit bounds for perturbed operands.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.6, 6.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.4.2–2.4.4

items.title: Balanced H and H² storage and matvec complexity
items.statement: Under explicit leaf-size, depth, block-count and interaction-list bounds, H storage and matvec work are O(k n log(2n/k)); nested H² storage and matvec work are O(k n).

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.6, 7.1, 9.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §§2.3.5, 2.4

items.title: Nested-basis H² multiplication is exact for its represented matrix
items.statement: The upward and downward transfer passes return exactly the represented H² matrix action.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), Chapter 9, §§9.1–9.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.6

items.title: Compressed block LU factors have a residual and inverse certificate
items.statement: Local Frobenius errors in compressed exact LU factors bound the global residual; if the inverse-scaled bound is below one, the approximate factor product is invertible with an explicit inverse error.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§6.2, 7.2
Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.5

title: Hierarchical low rank matrices and error propagation — Examples

items.title: A nearfield identity block requires full rank for subunit spectral error
items.statement: A diagonal two-point block is inadmissible and no rank-one approximation to the identity has spectral error below one.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.5–1.6

items.title: Two accepted local truncations can destroy positive definiteness after accumulation
items.statement: Two rank-one corrections, each within its own Frobenius tolerance, may be discarded before assembly and leave an indefinite approximate matrix.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, AdvNumCSE Lecture Document, Chapter 2, “Local Low-Rank Compression of Non-Local Operators” (ETH Zürich, AT’23), §2.4.5

items.title: A rank-one approximation of a separated Cauchy block
items.statement: For two points in each of two separated intervals, the first Cauchy expansion term gives an explicit rank-one block and exactly computable residual.

references.title: Steffen Börm, Lars Grasedyck, and Wolfgang Hackbusch, Hierarchical Matrices, MiS Lecture Note 21 (2003; revised June 2006), §§1.2–1.3
